title: DevX SDK feedback, canary & hotpatch cookbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: this cookbook documents a pragmatic, repeatable developer feedback loop for SDK releases and runtime canaries, plus an emergency hotpatch path targeted at short-duration production fixes for Redwood Inference SDKs and integration adapters. It is intended for SDK owners, DevEx engineers, oncall, and SREs.

Audience: SDK authors, build/release engineers, support engineers, oncall SREs, and product managers.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-fix regressions introduced by SDK changes or runtime adapter updates.
- Keep customer-impacting rollouts below the defined SLO churn budget.
- Provide a safe, audited hotpatch procedure for critical fixes with minimal blast radius.

When to use this doc
- Pre-release: when preparing canary cohorts for a patch or minor SDK release.
- During rollout: when telemetry gating flags cross thresholds.
- Incident: when a customer-facing regression is detected that can be corrected with a small code change in an SDK or adapter.

Ownership and roles
- SDK Owner: owns release artifacts, changelogs, and SDK regression tests.
- DevEx Canary Lead: defines canary cohorts and gating metrics, coordinates telemetry dashboards.
- Oncall SRE: watches alerts and decides on rollbacks or throttling.
- Support Triage Lead: coordinates customer communications and anchors root cause triage.

Key metrics and alerts (must be instrumented for every SDK & adapter change)
- API Error Rate (5m, per-customer and global): alert if 5m error rate > 0.5% and sustained > 3 minutes.
- Request Latency p95 (5m): alert if p95 increases by > 2x baseline for traffic-matched cohort.
- Token Cost Delta: alert if per-token CPU/GPU time increases by > 20% relative to baseline.
- Determinism / Golden Trace Drift: monitor example prompt suite mismatch rate; alert on > 3% mismatch for 30 minutes.
- Crash/oom rate: any crash loop or OOM > 1 incident/5m in canary hosts triggers immediate halt.

Canary strategy (recommended default)
1) Canary cohort composition - Small subset of inbound traffic: 1% of requests or 100 active sessions whichever is larger.
- Mix of synthetic and real traffic: 70% synthetic golden traces (deterministic prompts), 30% sampled real requests from low-risk tenants.
2) Duration & ramp plan - Minimum 30 minutes stable at each gate, preferred 2 hours for complex changes.
- Typical ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with at least one stable period between each jump.
3) Gating rules - Stop or rollback if any of the following occur for the canary cohort:
  a) API Error Rate tripped (see thresholds above)
  b) p95 latency > gate threshold
  c) Golden trace mismatch rate > 3% over 30 minutes
  d) Crash/oom observed
4) Canary promotion - To promote, SDK owner and DevEx Canary Lead sign off in the release tracker and record the canary run id.

Gating thresholds table (ASCII)
| Metric                        | Gate threshold (canary)               | Action on breach               | Owner         |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------|--------------------------------|---------------|
| API Error Rate (5m)          | > 0.5% sustained 3m                   | Pause rollout, rollback if persistent | Oncall SRE   |
| p95 latency (compared to baseline) | > 2x or +200 ms whichever smaller | Pause rollout, investigate      | DevEx Canary Lead |
| Golden trace mismatch rate   | > 3% over 30m                         | Revert to previous SDK, run debug harness | SDK Owner    |
| Token cost delta             | +20% CPU/GPU time                     | Halt promotion, contact infra   | Performance Eng |

Required telemetry & dashboards
- Canary dashboard per release: traffic mix, per-tenant error rates, latency heatmap, golden-trace pass/fail, top stack traces.
- Release run id must be tied to trace ids (trace sampling set to 100% for canary cohort).
- Telemetry retention: at least 48 hours of high-fidelity traces for canaries.

Procedures
A) Pre-canary checklist (SDK Owner)
1. Create release branch and build artifacts.
2. Run local regression golden-suite: all critical prompts must pass.
3. Submit release to CI: ensure canonical e2e smoke tests pass.
4. Update release tracker with planned canary cohorts and dash links.
5. Notify DevEx Canary Lead and create canary dashboard.
6. Tag the release with a run id and store in release metadata.

B) Starting a canary (DevEx Canary Lead)
1. Schedule the canary window and inform oncall and support (calendar + Slack #oncall).
2. Assign synthetic golden traces and low-risk tenant samples to the canary cohort.
3. Set trace sampling to 100% for cohort.
4. Start at 1% traffic, monitor the telemetry for the initial 30m.
5. If stable, follow ramp plan. Record checkpoints in the release tracker.

C) On alert breach (Oncall SRE)
1. Mark canary as paused in release tracker.
2. Triage using the triage checklist below.
3. If root cause is the new SDK change and cannot be mitigated quickly, rollback to previous version and open an incident.
4. If fix is small and safe, follow hotpatch path (see section D).

Triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
- Confirm alert validity (no noisy alerting artifact).
- Query top 5 stack traces and associated spans.
- Check golden trace failures and compare diffs.
- Identify whether failures are deterministic or data-dependent.
- If memory/cpu spikes are present, isolate by host pool and drain affected hosts.

Hotpatch path (fast, audited quickfix for SDK/adapter code)
Use this path only when: customer impact is high, the fix is small (<= 10 LOC or a config flip), and the risk of a full rollback is higher than the targeted fix.

Authorization & approvals
- Hotpatch must be approved by: SDK Owner + DevEx Canary Lead + Oncall SRE. Approval must be recorded in the release tracker.

Hotpatch steps (emergency)
1. Create a hotpatch branch from the current canary commit: e.g., hotfix/canary-<runid>-<short-desc>.
2. Implement the fix and include a unit test or behavioral regression test.
3. Run a focused CI suite (smoke + golden trace subset). CI may be allowed to short-circuit full suites for emergency hotpatches if the DevEx CI admin approves.
4. Build an artifact and tag as hotpatch-<runid>.
5. Deploy to canary cohort (do not deploy directly to 100% prod).
6. Monitor for at least 20 minutes at the same telemetry fidelity. If stable, follow a short ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 15–30 minute holds.
7. Document the change in the release tracker and create a short changelog entry.

Hotpatch rollback rules
- If hotpatch increases crash/oom, immediately revert to the previous canary artifact and open an incident with P0 tag.

Example commands and artifacts
- Create hotpatch branch:
  git checkout -b hotfix/canary-1234-fix-tokenize
- Local run of golden traces:
  ./scripts/run_golden_suite.sh --subset fast --artifact build/ark.tar.gz
- Deploy to canary via k8s rollout (example):
  kubectl set image deploy/sdk-adapter sdk-adapter=registry.redwood/adapter:hotpatch-1234 -n canary
- Query error rate (example PromQL):
  sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=adapter,release_run="1234",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=adapter,release_run="1234"}[5m])) > 0.005

SDK consumer-guidance snippets (for support & partner comms)
- If a quick fix is deployed, notify affected tenants and recommend temporary client-side mitigations (e.g., reduce batch size, add retry/backoff, pin to previous SDK minor version).
- Sample rollback notification template: 
  "We deployed a targeted fix to resolve <symptom>. If you continue to see <error>, please downgrade to SDK vX.Y.Z until we complete the broader remediation."

Incident post-hotpatch follow-up
- If hotpatch used, owner creates an abbreviated postmortem within 72 hours covering: timeline, root-cause, why hotpatch chosen over rollback, test coverage gaps, and next steps to prevent recurrence.
- Expand test suite with the failing golden trace and add to the release CI.

Common failure patterns and canonical fixes
1) Tokenization drift causing subtle mismatches - Symptom: golden-trace diffs where only token boundaries differ.
- Fix: lock tokenizer version in adapter, add round-trip tokenization tests.
2) Backcompat-breaking default changed in SDK args - Symptom: downstream errors after upgrade.
- Fix: reintroduce deprecated default for one release, notify deprecation, and schedule migration.
3) Increased latency caused by lazy-init on first request - Symptom: initial p95 spike for a cohort.
- Fix: warmup probes during rollout and add init-time telemetry to CI.
4) Memory leak in streaming path - Symptom: OOMs after sustained streaming traffic.
- Fix: add leak detector, increase cadence of canary host restarts until root cause fixed.

Testing & CI recommendations
- Add golden trace unit tests to the primary sdk repo and gate PRs. Use a small stable seed of deterministic prompts.
- CI should provide a fast smoke target that can be run manually by DevEx leads for hotpatch verification.
- For larger changes, use the integration harness that mirrors the canary traffic mix.

Documentation & communication
- All canary runs, hotpatch approvals, and rollbacks must be recorded in the release tracker ticket.
- Create a short notes blurb for the customer-facing status page when a canary triggers and a hotpatch is in progress.

Appendix A: Minimal debug checklist for support engineers (5-minute read)
1. Identify affected tenants and their SDK version.
2. Determine whether issue surfaced in canary cohort only.
3. Pull golden-trace diffs and attach to ticket.
4. If fixable by pinning or client workaround, provide step-by-step instructions.
5. If not, escalate to SDK Owner and open canary run incident.

Appendix B: Example release metadata JSON (store in release tracker)
{
  "release_run": "1234",
  "artifact": "registry.redwood/sdk:2.1.0-hotpatch-1234",
  "canary_cohort": "1%-synthetic-70%-real-30%",
  "gates": "error_rate<0.5%|p95<2x|golden_mismatch<3%",
  "approvals": "aisha.patel, marcus.nguyen, sofia.martinez"
}

Notes and links
- See also: SDK release policy, Canary dashboard template, Telemetry schema (internal links in related pages).
- Contact: #devx-canaries (Slack) or paging oncall SRE for P0s.
